title: How far to split an interface

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, how should the methods of a fat interface be grouped when it is split up?

options.text: By the clients that call them, one interface per client role
options.says: The page says to group methods by client usage and create one interface per client cluster.

options.text: By the fields they touch, one interface per implementation part
options.says: The page says to group methods by client usage, not by implementation similarity.

options.text: By each single method, one interface for every method listed
options.says: The page calls that over-segregation: interfaces so granular no client uses just one.

questions.stem: Per this page, what do Java's default methods do for an interface that has grown fat?

options.text: They soften it, but leave clients tied to every method
options.says: The page says default methods partially mitigate fat interfaces but do not solve the coupling.

options.text: They cure it, as clients then rely on no unused method
options.says: The page says default methods do not solve the fundamental coupling problem.

options.text: They block it, as the compiler caps how many it may hold
options.says: The page says default methods allow adding methods to an interface without breaking implementations.

concepts: Default methods can soften a fat interface but do not remove the coupling of its clients to every method.
Methods are grouped into interfaces by the clients that use them together, neither one fat interface nor one interface per method.
